summary: Milestone 2026.09.662 completed 12 experiments (3 compute-bound and 9 synthesis-only) in 18.3 wall-time minutes. The longest task was the synthesis-only 'Measure delayed proper-loss learning and durable retained decisions' at 7.31 minutes, while the longest compute-bound task was 'Seal descriptive source roles and delayed-feedback decision tests' at 1.63 minutes. Sub-phase timing was not recorded within these runs to separate model inference duration or synthesis computation from validation scaffolding and artifact serialization overhead.
bottlenecks_identified: 'Measure delayed proper-loss learning and durable retained decisions' was the longest task at 7.31 minutes out of 18.3 total wall-time minutes (approx. 40% of milestone duration), but as a synthesis-only task without granular sub-phase timers, CPU code generation cannot be isolated from validation scaffolding or artifact serialization.

Intra-task phase durations were unrecorded for the compute-bound experiments ('Seal descriptive source roles and delayed-feedback decision tests' at 1.63 minutes and 'Qualify owned Qwen transport and live-panel budget with a bounded canary' at 1.25 minutes), preventing isolation of GPU inference latency from verification scaffolding and file serialization.

The top 5 experiments accounted for 13.74 out of 18.3 total wall-time minutes (approx. 75% of execution time), with milestone timings reconstructed from disk mtimes rather than continuous runtime execution logging.

The GPU monitor report provides an isolated post-completion snapshot (PID 772157 on GPU 0 with 18054MB allocated at 0% utilization, GPU 1 idle at 4MB), leaving GPU utilization across active compute execution windows unmeasured (with gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks locked to false).
Task launch records did not log model concurrency or runner dispatch details, although all completed tasks were single-model runs where DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch is not applicable.
improvements_suggested: Instrument granular sub-phase duration timers and monotonic stage logging inside synthesis-only and compute-bound workflows to isolate code generation and model inference latency from verification scaffolding and disk serialization.

Deploy continuous, task-aligned accelerator telemetry during compute-bound executions to sample live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active compute windows rather than relying on point-in-time post-run snapshots.
Record explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment task receipts to audit DualGPURunner eligibility whenever two or more models run concurrently.
Implement runtime milestone-scoped execution logging to avoid reliance on post-hoc disk-mtime timing reconstruction.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument sub-phase duration timers and per-stage progress logging inside the proper-loss learning and runner requalification pipelines.
Deploy continuous accelerator telemetry during compute-bound task execution to record live GPU utilization and VRAM occupancy across active execution windows.
Emit explicit model concurrency and runner dispatch metadata in experiment receipts to audit DualGPURunner engagement on multi-model workloads.
meta_reflection: The milestone completed 12 experiments (3 compute-bound and 9 synthesis-only) in 18.3 wall-time minutes, with wall time led by the synthesis-only task 'Measure delayed proper-loss learning and durable retained decisions' (7.31 minutes) and the compute-bound task 'Seal descriptive source roles and delayed-feedback decision tests' (1.63 minutes). The post-run GPU monitor report confirms an idle llama.cpp process on GPU 0 after completion but cannot evaluate active-window compute efficiency, and because only single-model tasks were executed, no DualGPURunner multi-model dispatch opportunity was missed. Sub-phase timing and continuous execution telemetry are necessary next steps to identify actionable latency optimizations.
